explanation: Safe cities established to provide protection for those who unintentionally killed someone, so they could seek asylum and avoid vengeance from the victim's family.
The main character in the book of Joshua, who succeeded Moses as leader of the people of Israel and led them into the promised land of Canaan.
Another designation for God, the almighty Creator, who plays a central role in the book of Joshua and gives guidance and instructions to Joshua and the people of Israel.
The area that God promised to give to the people of Israel as their inheritance and homeland. This area corresponds roughly to present-day Israel, Palestine, Lebanon, and parts of Jordan and Syria.
A person who seeks to avenge the killing of a family member by killing the perpetrator. In Joshua 20, cities of refuge are established to protect killers from avengers of blood.
The prophet and leader of the people of Israel before Joshua, who received the Ten Commandments from God and led the people out of Egypt and through the wilderness.
